title: Higurashi WHEN THEY CRY: Curse Killing Arc
label: Quick read (from summaries)
premise: In the mountain village of Hinamizawa, Keiichi Maebara grows close to the youngest of his friends, Satoko, whose brother vanished a year earlier. When her abusive uncle returns, Keiichi tries to protect her, turns to a plan to kill the uncle, and is drawn into paranoia as rumors of Oyashiro-sama's curse close in. The third 'question' arc of the Higurashi manga (Yen Press blurb via MU; Manga Bookshelf review).
life_message: Trying to fix abuse alone through violence and secrecy leads to ruin; trust in friends matters.

content.note: Murder plan and killing, corpses, 'a huge pile of body bags'; gore appears 'when it needs to' (review; MU Murder/s, Death).
Psychological horror, curse, paranoia, oppressive mood (review; AniList Horror, Psychological).
No romance noted; reviewer warns of 'lolicon character designs'.

dominant: Vigilante 'greater good' killing critiqued; village curse; powerlessness of children

Dignity vs honor.evidence: Keiichi answers abuse personally rather than through authorities (review).

Order vs freedom.evidence: Close-knit rural village with strong customs (AniList Rural; MU Rural Town).

Civic vs kin.evidence: Protecting Satoko as a 'big brother'; clan loyalties of the village (MU blurb).

Equality vs hierarchy.evidence: Village power and elders loom over children (to verify).

Tradition vs secular-rational.evidence: Oyashiro-sama curse and village myth central (AniList Mythology).

Survival vs self-expression.evidence: Survival and safety under threat dominate (review).

folkways.japan: A closed rural Japanese village with a guardian-deity festival and strong group loyalties frames the story; these customs are setting, not endorsed.

delivery.evidence: Reviewer frames Keiichi's choices as failures driven by 'paranoia and fear'; no moralizing noted (Manga Bookshelf).
delivery.note: The lesson emerges from Keiichi's failed choices rather than speeches.

winners_losers: No one wins: the arc ends in mass death; Satoko and Keiichi receive sympathy while the abusive uncle is shown as 'loathsome'.
